reason: Start with the mast on the base so there is a frame to brace against sideways bending.
expectation: I expect the uprights and crosspiece to attach to the base, leaving the frame ready for braces.

alternatives.reason: The pulley will likely be useful later, but the goal points first toward the frame.

effect: The mast is now upright on the base, ready to brace.
reason: Diagonal braces should stiffen the mast against sideways bending, matching the goal.
expectation: I expect the braces to attach to the mast and make the frame more rigid.

alternatives.reason: The pulley looks useful for lifting later, but bracing addresses the current goal.

effect: The braces make the mast harder to distort sideways; the crane still needs other parts.
reaction: The rectangle-to-diamond explanation makes the braces' purpose clear.
reason: Prepare the boom and hinge so the crane can eventually support a lifting arm.
expectation: I expect the hinge pin to fit into the boom, ready to attach it to the mast.

alternatives.reason: The pulley also needs assembly, but I chose to prepare the boom first.

effect: The boom now has a hinge pin and can be attached to the braced mast.
reason: Attach the boom to continue building the crane frame.
expectation: I expect the hinged boom to attach to the mast, though it may need additional support.

alternatives.reason: The pulley also needs assembly, but attaching the boom seems more directly relevant to the frame.

effect: The boom is attached to the braced mast, but it may still need support.
reaction: The hinged frame is taking shape, though this was a predictable fitting.
reason: Add the stay to support the boom and continue building the frame.
expectation: I expect the stay to hold the boom in position; the frame may still need stabilizing feet.

alternatives.reason: The pulley will likely help with lifting, but the boom support seems more relevant to the current goal.

effect: The stay now holds the boom; the pulley is the only offered combination.
reaction: The support is in place as expected.
reason: Assemble the pulley, following the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the wheel to fit into the fork on its axle, ready to guide a lifting line.

effect: The pulley is assembled, and I understand that it redirects the pull rather than reducing the weight.
reaction: The distinction between changing direction and reducing force is useful.
reason: Attach the pulley to the boom; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the pulley to fit onto the boom, ready to guide a rope.

effect: The pulley is now at the boom tip, and the feet are the only offered combination.
reason: Add the spreading feet to stabilize the crane frame.
expectation: I expect the feet to widen the base and make the crane less likely to tip.

effect: The spreading feet widened the crane’s footprint, and the completed braced frame resisted Jo’s gentle nudge. The chapter’s goal is complete.
reaction: The final test tied the construction together, though the basket is still waiting to be lifted.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the diagonal braces was most worthwhile: the explanation showed clearly why triangles resist the sideways distortion that turns a rectangle into a diamond.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the hinge pin and then attaching the boom felt predictable and added little explanation on their own.

surprise.text: The fixed pulley’s explanation clarified that it changes the pull’s direction without halving the weight.

arbitrary.text: Assembling and fitting the pulley made sense for a crane, but felt somewhat tangential to the stated goal of resisting sideways bending.

continue.text: I would continue to see the crane lift the basket; the explanations of bracing and the pulley made the mechanism worth exploring, even if several fittings were routine.
